title: Add imported-task review metadata and a backlog triage workflow in /tasks
description:
Problem: the imported `tracker-import` backlog entered `Data/Tasks` as durable records, but the task model does not yet make vetting status, stale-task disposition, or review ownership explicit. This leaves imported tasks looking equally trustworthy even when some are obsolete and others were never expanded beyond placeholder notes.

Desired outcome:
- Imported or machine-ingested tasks can be reviewed, marked vetted, archived as obsolete, or flagged for rewrite without relying on ad hoc manual inspection.
- `/tasks` exposes enough provenance and review state to keep the backlog trustworthy over time.

Implementation plan:
1. Define the minimum provenance/review fields or conventions needed for imported tasks.
2. Decide whether review state lives in first-class fields, labels, comments, or a hybrid model.
3. Add UI affordances and documentation for reviewing, archiving, or rewriting imported tasks.
4. Add tests covering import provenance display and review-state persistence.

Acceptance criteria:
- An imported task can be distinguished from a user-authored task at a glance.
- A reviewer can mark a task as vetted or obsolete without freeform conventions only.
- The review outcome survives reload and is queryable.

Validation:
- Exercise the workflow on at least one imported task.
- Add focused tests for review metadata persistence and filtering.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from the 2026-05-24 codebase audit after vetting the imported tracker backlog.

comments.body: Review round: completed. Added imported-task triage actions in /tasks (vetted, needs-rewrite, obsolete/archive) with persisted labels and audit comments.
